evals.prompt: I want to study English from this YouTube video about Claude Code Agent Teams: https://youtu.be/vDVSGVpB2vc. The transcript has already been downloaded and cleaned — it's at evals/files/transcript_clean.txt. Please follow the skill's workflow and generate video_notes.md in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: A video_notes.md file with Part 1 containing at least 15 English expressions (each with Expression, Meaning, Example, and In the video fields), and Part 2 containing a structured content summary of the video's technical subject.
expectations: Part 1 contains at least 15 numbered expression entries
Each expression entry has all four fields: Expression, Meaning, Example, and 'In the video'
The 'In the video' quotes are drawn from the transcript (e.g. words like 'agent', 'teammate', 'shoot off', 'token', 'QA' appear in quotes)
Part 2 is present and contains numbered ### section headings
The header includes the source URL https://youtu.be/vDVSGVpB2vc

evals.prompt: Make me English learning notes from this tech video. Clean transcript is at evals/files/transcript_clean.txt. The video is https://youtu.be/vDVSGVpB2vc — it's about Claude Code agent teams. Output to video_notes.md.
evals.expected_output: A correctly structured video_notes.md. Expressions should be informal/idiomatic (not obvious vocabulary), examples should be original sentences unrelated to Claude/AI, and the content summary should use tables or structured lists where appropriate.
expectations: Part 1 expressions are idiomatic or colloquial (e.g. 'spin up', 'burn through', 'under the hood', 'from the jump') rather than plain technical vocabulary
Each Example sentence is set in a scenario unrelated to Claude or AI agents
Part 2 uses at least one markdown table
Entry separators (---) appear between every expression in Part 1
